name: Signs a Retaining Wall Is Failing

mainEntity.name: What are the signs a retaining wall in Los Angeles County is failing?
mainEntity.text: What are the signs a retaining wall in Los Angeles County is failing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early signs of retaining wall failure are often visible before collapse occurs. Look for outward leaning, curved or bulging sections, cracks in the face of the wall, open joints, settlement at the base, water staining, pooling behind the wall, or new gaps where soil is escaping. On hillside properties, these symptoms can worsen quickly after heavy rain or prolonged irrigation. In Los Angeles County, drainage and slope conditions make it important to act early because a failing wall can affect nearby fences, patios, driveways, or structures. A contractor should determine whether the wall can be repaired, partially rebuilt, or needs full replacement. If the wall is moving, the most important question is not cosmetic repair but what is causing the pressure and whether the drainage system is functioning.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common failure signs include leaning, bulging, cracked blocks or concrete, separating joints, sinking at the base, water pooling behind the wall, and fresh soil spilling through gaps. These warning signs often point to drainage failure, weak footing, or soil pressure issues. A contractor should inspect the wall quickly before movement gets worse.
